docs.text: A thinly veiled guise. Brains are a funny thing. My brain runs on praise, but is awkward about accepting praise. It wants to share things I do, but also won't allow me to do so without layers of abstraction. This is one of them. I cannot advertise my work myself, either blogs or podcasts or books. But what I can do is invent Patched Atlas, which is an extension of the nom-de-plume idea. It acts as a buffer between myself and my work, so I can freely advertise it without feeling like I'm boasting or bragging or begging for attention. Brains are a funny thing. This is just how I hack mine.

docs.text: Written Works of Dorian Roland Gone Dark A former soldier turned cyber sleuth, known only as Narrator, belongs to a secret online society dedicated to unraveling the mysteries of the Net of Lights; an AI system capable of predicting human behavior on a global scale. When the system suddenly loses track of half the population it monitors, Narrator is drawn into a covert race to uncover the cause while keeping the AI’s existence hidden from the world. As he follows a trail of deception stretching back decades, he becomes entangled between powerful corporate and military interests, unsure whom to trust. To uncover the truth, he must expose the forces behind the Net of Lights, understand its true purpose, and decide whether the knowledge it offers is worth the price of possessing it.
